title: Capacity commitments approval matrix and forecasting protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers buying Dedicated capacity need a deterministic, auditable flow that ties capacity reservation types (committed, burst, spot) to throughput guarantees, pricing tiers, and autoscaling behavior. Currently intake is ad-hoc: sales and solutions engineering manually negotiate qps/slots and finance issues ad-hoc invoices. That causes overprovisioning, missed SLOs, confusing handoffs, and unclear rollback/fallback options when capacity is constrained.

Goal: Design a provisioning protocol and approval matrix that standardizes: 1) reservation intake fields (expected throughput, peak percentiles, retention windows, redundancy zone requirements), 2) approval matrix (who signs off at each commitment level and SLA), 3) autoscaling policy mappings for each reservation type, 4) forecast cadence and the escalation path when projected capacity delta > 20% of reserved baseline.

Acceptance criteria: 
- A published intake form schema (fields + required validation) that both Sales and Solutions can use.
- An approval matrix mapping reservation bands to approvers (e.g., up to 100 qps: Solutions Engineer; 100-1k qps: PM + Solutions; >1k qps: VP Sales + Finance + SRE).
- Autoscaling policy templates for each reservation type (committed, burst, spot) including min/max pool sizes, burst windows, and fallback model routing rules.
- Forecasting protocol: weekly rolling 12-week capacity forecasts with variance bands, owner, and dashboard link.
- Billing & finance handshake: documented commitment billing triggers and early-termination implications.
- Implementation plan with required engineering tickets and spec links.

Scope exclusions: detailed pricing negotiation playbooks, per-customer legal contract language (handled by GTM/Legal).
comments: 2026-02-16 — Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed to make the intake schema machine-readable (JSON schema) to allow automated validation at signup and manual overrides for enterprise deals. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Capacity+Intake+Kickoff
2026-02-19 — Miguel Santos: Initial draft approval bands proposed in the doc. Flag: SRE input required for burst/fallback rules. Assigned ENG-2045 to prototype autoscale mapping.

2026-02-24 — Priya Rao (Finance): Suggested adding mid-tier financial guardrails for multi-quarter commitments; added finance signoff in 500-2k qps band. Recommends pre-authorized credit limit for transient burst billing. See spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/finance-models/redwood-cap-commit-2026

2026-03-02 — Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Reviewed autoscale templates, suggested hard cap for burst windows (max 15 minutes) and mandatory circuit-breaker routing to compatible model-variants. Assigned ENG-2110 for a KV-cache capacity test to validate durable throughput under fallback routing.

2026-03-08 — Design review (DES-337): UX spec for reservation intake form updated to include telemetry consent checkbox, region affinity, and optional estimated token distribution. Link: https://drive.google.com/designs/capacity-intake
2026-03-10 — Asha Patel: Incorporated feedback from Finance and SRE; ready for stakeholder review. Next: legal sign-off and one pilot with existing mid-market customer (Acme AI) for validation.
decision_log: Decisions so far: 1) Use 3 reservation bands (Committed, Flexible-Burst, Spot) with clear autoscale templates. 2) Require Finance signoff for any multi-quarter commitments > 500 qps or monthly spend > $75k. 3) Autoscale templates will include a mandatory circuit-breaker to fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant when pool allocation fails. Trade-offs: stricter approval matrix reduces risk but adds friction in sales cycle; agreed to pilot with two customers before finalizing.
next_steps: 1) Ship JSON schema for intake form (owner: Design + PM) by 2026-03-17. 2) ENG to implement autoscale policy templates and create simulation (ENG-2045, ENG-2110). 3) Finance & Legal to review billing triggers and contract clauses (target 2026-03-24). 4) Pilot run with Acme AI (point of contact: Taylor Kim) in April.
notes_for_engineering: Engineering needs: API for intake submission + validation, mapping engine from reservation to autoscale template, dashboard telemetry for forecast variance, and a feature flag to enable circuit-breaker routing during the pilot. Performance budget: no more than 5% added latency in routing decision path. See ENG-2045 and ENG-2110.
estimated_cost_impact: Estimated monthly committed spend buckets: small (up to $10k), mid ($10k-$75k), large (>$75k). Forecasting protocol should reduce overprovisioning by 12-18% in pilot, per initial finance model.
